Wee Hur makes student housing foray in Singapore with 1,398 new beds at NTU
article:
Wee Hur Holdings Ltd is entering Singapore’s purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA) scene — building on its experience in the segment across Australia and Hong Kong.

It will design, build, finance, operate and maintain a new property with about 1,398-beds at Nanyang Technology University's (NTU) main campus in the west of Singapore.

The property will house mainly postgraduate students, with a limited number of beds for undergraduates. It will be the first asset in Singapore managed under Y Suites, Wee Hur’s PBSA brand.

NTU has issued a letter of award for the project in respect of the Singapore-listed company’s proposal submitted on Sept 13, after an expression-of-interest and request-for-proposal process.

The award is subject to terms and conditions, and the parties are working towards finalising the definitive agreement for the project, Wee Hur said in an Oct 16 release.

Construction is targeted to begin in the third quarter of 2027, before operations are expected to commence by the start of the 2029/2030 academic year. That is subject to the relevant NTU and regulatory approvals.

When completed, the PBSA is expected to be Singapore’s largest privately developed and operated student accommodation facility within an autonomous university campus.

It will sit next to 30 Nanyang Link, the university’s former Hall of Residence 7, which is temporarily housing students from Hall of Residence 1 while the latter undergoes renovation.

The greenfield site for the new PBSA measures about 6,000 sq m (64,583 sq ft).

An initial 20-year land lease will be granted, with an option to extend for two five-year terms, subject to the terms and conditions of the definitive agreement.

Wee Hur has experience across the PBSA lifecycle, spanning greenfield development, construction, investment and operations.

Goh Chengyu, CEO, Wee Hur Property, noted that the NTU project adds to the group's development pipeline, provides further visibility to its construction activities and, when completed, will contribute a long-term recurring income stream.

Goh Wee Ping, Wee Hur Holdings chief investment officer and Wee Hur Capital CEO, said: "Having established our PBSA platform in Australia and expanded into Hong Kong, bringing Y Suites home to Singapore marks an important step in our ambition to build a regional PBSA platform across Asia Pacific."

title: Exxon signals record refining earnings on soaring diesel prices
article:
(Oct 16): ExxonMobil Holdings Corp is the latest oil supermajor to signal soaring third-quarter refining profits as wars in the Persian Gulf and Russia crippled fuel-making facilities causing prices to surge.

 

Higher refining margins added about US$4.5 billion to ExxonMobil’s results, the company said in a preliminary earnings statement on Friday. That’s on top of the US$4.1 billion the company made from refining in the second quarter.

After accounting for other items, analysts are expecting ExxonMobil’s refining earnings to be about US$7.8 billion in the third quarter, which would be the company’s highest on record, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

North America’s biggest oil producer is scheduled to report its full results on Oct 30. ExxonMobil shares rose as much as 1.5% on Friday.

European supermajors have also indicated strong refining margins after fuel production became a critical pinch-point amid broader energy market disruptions amid the US-Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts. The loss of production in these regions means fuels like diesel are in short supply globally, driving up prices. ExxonMobil runs the world’s largest refining system outside of China.

The Gulf Coast 3-2-1 crack spread, an indication of US refining profitability, was 28% higher in the quarter on a sequential basis, touching a record US$72.64 on Sept 22. US retail prices for diesel, used in heavy-duty transportation and farm equipment, touched a record US$6.53 a gallon last month.

See also: IEA agrees to release of outstanding 100 mil barrels of oil

ExxonMobil’s surging profits will be partly offset by lower oil prices, which reduced profits by about US$1.3 billion. It will also take a US$2.5 billion hit due to “timing effects”, or derivative positions linked to cargoes that have been shipped but not yet delivered.

Chief executive officer Darren Woods has invested heavily in ExxonMobil’s refineries over the past decade, leaving it well-placed to take advantage of current prices. Previously the company’s refining boss, Woods spent billions of dollars upgrading and expanding refineries in Texas, Singapore, Belgium and the UK.

title: Bukit Sembawang to acquire Kallang Distripark land from other Lee-family entities for $196 mil
article:
Bukit Sembawang Estates is paying $196.04 million to buy over a 51,000 sqm site along the Kallang River from a group of entities including Lee Rubber.

With a lease upgrading premium to secure a fresh 99-year lease, and also land betterment charges and other expenses, Bt Sembawang expects a total land cost of $1.01 billion.

Savills, which has been commissioned to put a value to the land, estimates that this plot to be worth $1.007 billion on a "vacant land" basis and to have a gross development value of $2.031 billion.

The land is now occupied by a cluster of unused warehouses, harking back to the years when the physical trading of commodities was a leading business activity of Singapore and Lee Rubber a leading player in this industry.

Both Bt Sembawang and Lee Rubber and their related entities are controlled by the Lee family that is better known for their stake in Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp.

Lee Chien Shih, Bt Sembawang's non-executive and non-independent director since 1999, is linked to Tropical Warehousing, the entity which now holds the site. Tropical Warehousing, in turn, is held by Tropical Produce Company, whose shareholders including various Lee family-linked entities.

See also: IOI Properties Group tightens grip on Singapore’s CBD

As such, this is deemed an interested party transaction.

Bt Sembawang plans to develop a residential development with commercial first-storey use on around half the total land area and also undertake infrastructure works on the remaining half.

With a gross plot ratio of 3, the proposed residential development will have a permissible gross floor area of around 74,707.41 sqm.

title: Apple iPhone Duo orders slip into 2027 amid pre-order frenzy
article:
(Oct 16): Shipping estimates for Apple Inc’s first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, slipped into December and beyond within minutes of the company opening pre-orders on Friday.

The extended timelines suggest that strong demand and sharply constrained supply will make the US$1,999 device challenging to purchase on its Oct 23 release date or in the near future.

The latest shipping estimates shown on Apple’s online store applied to both colours of the iPhone Duo, and in all storage configurations, ranging from 256 gigabytes (GB) to two terabytes.

Pre-order customers reported delayed delivery dates even after taking Apple’s recommended steps of reserving their preferred colour and storage size ahead of time in an attempt to speed up the buying process.

Apple retail stores also ran out of launch-day stock of the iPhone Duo, the company’s first-ever foldable device, almost instantly after pre-orders began at 8am in New York.

Bloomberg Intelligence analysts Anurag Rana and Josh Christensen said in a note on Friday that iPhone Duo sales could exceed their earlier estimates of 14 million units and US$28 billion in sales for the company’s fiscal 2027 year. If Apple can convince current Pro and Pro Max owners to switch to the base version of the foldable, they added, that would push up the iPhone’s average selling price by 82% and 67%, respectively.

See also: Taiwan to fund US$4 bil Texas industrial complex for AI, Nvidia partners

Shares of Apple rose as much as 1.7% to US$347.82 in New York before paring some of those gains. The stock was up 0.7% at 10.36am.

Compared with the debut of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in September, which went smoothly for customers who placed a timely order, securing an iPhone Duo was significantly more difficult. Apple is set to sell about six million units of the iPhone Duo this year, Counterpoint Research said last month.

Apple typically reserves some units for walk-in customers on release day, which could revive the long lines outside Apple and mobile carrier stores that were once an annual tradition for iPhone launches.

title: US chipmakers set for longest losing streak since 2008
article:
(Oct 16): The final stretch of a jittery week on Wall Street saw stocks wavering amid an ongoing selloff in chipmakers that has left investors questioning the prospects for the artificial-intelligence (AI) trade.

While most shares in the S&P 500 rose, the gauge fluctuated. A rout in chip giants dragged into an eighth straight day — the longest losing streak since 2008. CoreWeave Inc tumbled 7.5%, resuming a selloff that’s been fuelled by concerns over whether the massive buildout of AI infrastructure has outrun the ability of companies to get a return on their investments.

Those worries revived safe-haven flows into the treasury market, with bonds paring their losses. Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh’s remarks did little to alter the outlook for rates. In a moderated discussion on Friday morning in Bangkok at the International Monetary Fund’s annual meetings, he reiterated that the Fed will deliver price stability.

“The most interesting event this week was not the inflation data or the Fed commentary but the market’s reaction,” said Brian Jacobsen at Annex Wealth Management. “When several AI-related stocks pulled back, investors moved money into healthcare, financials, materials, and smaller companies, which held up comparatively well.”

Risk aversion is set to dominate markets in coming weeks as investors seek shelter from the AI trade, higher interest rates and volatility around US midterm elections, according to Bank of America Corp.’s Michael Hartnett.

See also: US stocks fall on inflation woes as chip rout deepens

Some of the main moves in markets:

See also: Stocks bounce from lows on Williams’ rate remarks
• The S&P 500 was little changed as of 10.04am New York time
• The Japanese yen rose 0.2% to 157.76 per dollar
• The yield on 10-year Treasuries advanced two basis points to 5.07%
• Germany’s 10-year yield was little changed at 3.41%

title: RegCo queries SGX-listed Indonesian agri firms on cause and impact of haze
article:
SGX RegCo, which sets ESG standards for Singapore-listed companies, has "engaged" with various Indonesia-based agriculture companies.

Among others, the exchange's frontline regulator wants information on the impact of the fires on their operations, if their activities may have contributed to the haze, and how they are responding.

"SGX RegCo takes the ongoing forest and peatland fires seriously, given the impact of the haze on communities, the environment and businesses," says SGX RegCo.

SGX RegCo says that it has strengthened ESG disclosure and reporting standards, improving issuers’ disclosure on environmental policies, risks and practices, and enhancing accountability.

"We note that some companies have already made announcements on the current haze situation. These include their operational policies and fire prevention measures, including ‘no burning’ policy, ‘no peat’ policy, hotspot monitoring and water management," notes the regulator.

They include First Resources, Golden Agri-Resources, Indofood Agri Resources, Wilmar International, Bumitama Agri and Kencana Agri.

See also: Singapore haze hits highest level as Indonesian fires worsen

"Listed companies are expected to disclose material information in a timely and transparent manner, manage their material ESG risks and provide relevant disclosures in their sustainability reports.

"We also expect issuers to keep stakeholders informed as the situation develops. SGX RegCo will take appropriate regulatory action where companies fail to meet their disclosure obligations under the SGX Listing Rules,” says the RegCo.

title: Ueda ‘can’t tolerate’ underlying inflation further over 2%
article:
(Oct 16): Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Kazuo Ueda said he “can’t tolerate” underlying inflation rising further above 2%.

“Going forward, underlying inflation is already roughly around 2%, and we cannot tolerate it rising any further,” Ueda told reporters on Friday when asked if prices nearing the bank’s target will have any impact on policy management.

“The policy phase has recently shifted towards making sure inflation settles at around 2% as a key objective,” he said.

Ueda spoke after attending a series of international meetings of financial chiefs and central bankers in Bangkok.

Ueda’s comments come as investors closely scrutinize the BOJ’s trajectory, following its September rate hike. His remarks signalled greater caution over inflation — suggesting the need for the bank to raise borrowing costs at a pace that would keep it from falling behind the curve.

Earlier this week, Bloomberg reported that BOJ officials are leaning against raising rates for a second consecutive meeting later this month, while keeping open the possibility of another move as soon as December, citing people familiar with the matter. Price developments have been broadly in line with the BOJ’s projections, with underlying inflation expected to reach a level consistent with its 2% target sometime in the next 18 months, the people said.

See also: The Nobel Prize in economics is a message to the Fed

In September, the BOJ raised rates for the second time in three months, marking its fastest pace of monetary tightening since 1990.

Ueda said that his discussions with international counterparts hadn’t yielded much significant information that contradicted the BOJ’s current assessment. He added that he would discuss with fellow board members at the October meeting whether to tweak the bank’s current language describing underlying inflation as nearing its 2% target.

On Thursday, BOJ board member Junko Koeda warned against too much caution over raising interest rates, also hinting at another rate hike in coming months.

See also: BOE’s Bailey sees little evidence of second-round inflation

Overnight swaps have suggested that traders are pricing in less than 5% probability of a hike this month, with the chances rising to about 75% for a move by December.

About a third of economists polled last month forecast a move in December, with more than half predicting the BOJ would wait until January.

title: UniCredit gets ECB go-ahead to take control of Commerzbank
article:
(Oct 16): UniCredit SpA won approval from the European Central Bank (ECB) for its increased Commerzbank AG stake, paving the way for chief executive officer Andrea Orcel to take over the German lender.

 

The green light from the ECB means the Italian bank can raise its stake above 30% and potentially hold as much as 100% of Commerzbank, the bank said in a statement on Thursday.

The decision marks “an important milestone” in the acquisition of Commerzbank, UniCredit said. It will “be able to take control of the bank” around the end of the year.

It’s another win for Orcel, who has been pursuing Commerzbank publicly since September 2024, despite vocal opposition from the German government and the lender’s management. The acquisition of a firm valued at about €42 billion would be among the largest banking deals globally in two decades.

The supervisor’s nod, while widely expected, was one of the most significant regulatory hurdles preventing UniCredit from taking ownership of the Commerzbank shares tendered to it in a takeover offer earlier this year. Once the few remaining approvals have come in as well, Orcel will control almost 50% of Commerzbank’s voting rights, effectively giving him an majority at shareholder meetings and the ability to implement at least some of his far-reaching plans for the German lender.

As part of that plan, Orcel has indicated he’ll seek to replace swathes of Commerzbank’s supervisory board and subsequently the top management including CEO Bettina Orlopp. He’s already looking for potential candidates to succeed her, people familiar with the matter have said.

See also: Sumitomo Life CEO targets acquisitions in Southeast Asia, US

UniCredit still needs approvals from European Union antitrust authorities, the US Federal Reserve and the relevant Polish regulator. Commerzbank has a large subsidiary named mBank in Poland.

“The remaining regulatory processes and conditions to complete the offer for Commerzbank are expected around year-end,” UniCredit said in the statement.

Asked about her future at Commerzbank in a Bloomberg TV interview on Wednesday, Orlopp said her contract runs until 2029 and she will seek to serve it out for as long as she’s got backing from the supervisory board and agreement on strategy.

See also: IHH said to join race for TPG’s Malaysian hospitals

Taking control of Commerzbank will probably also mean that the ECB will count the lender as a subsidiary of UniCredit for supervisory purposes, a move that will lead to higher capital requirements for the Italian bank. Orlopp said in the interview that accounting “consolidation” will take place “for the full year 2026 or for the first quarter of 2027.”

The Italian lender has held talks about Commerzbank’s future with the German government, which owns about 13% of the lender. Berlin expects commitments on preserving the bank’s stock-market listing and its Frankfurt base, as well as guarantees on jobs and the business with small and mid-sized companies.

German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said on the sidelines of the IMF’s annual meetings in Bangkok that he hadn’t seen any official documents on the ECB decision regarding Commerzbank yet and couldn’t comment. He reaffirmed Germany’s demands and said the talks with UniCredit about them are continuing.

Speaking to reporters in Bangkok, Italy’s Finance Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti said that UniCredit’s pursuit of Commerzbank has been a success, but there is still work to be done.
